question: P4 run-01: which remedies and rule interpretations should run-02 use?

decisions.topic: feet slide in locomotion and stance-changing transitions

options.A1: stance-foot lock (two-bone leg IK) in the runtime evaluator and the Blender check, verified by the same closed loop; about 2-3 h
options.A2: accept the slide of in-place cross-fades as a V1 limitation (relaxes the feet gate for those pairs)
options.A3: author start/stop transition clips (new clips; larger scope)

options.B1: exempt the coat when every bed-clip layer that drives the legs is inside its seated window (non-bed layers neutral): extends entries 19-20 to transitions
options.B2: keep strict: those samples stay failing

options.C1: a fade may not overlap a socket or bed-support event of either clip: entry fades finish before the target's first event, exit fades start after the source's last event (non-loop clips hold their last frame); combinations that cannot fit are shortened to fit and listed
options.C2: keep the timing: the 400 ms x 1.5 combinations stay failing

decisions.recommended: decide after run-02 (A and C change the leg poses and remove the long-fade cases)

options.D1: fix the armpit and hip-crease folds in the foundation (b21) and re-verify every clip; hours
options.D2: keep the gate strict and list the remaining cases as V1 known issues
options.D3: judge transition collapse only on triangles that are non-degenerate and unfolded in every active source clip at that time, listing the rest as foundation issues (gate-scope change)

options.keep: playback speed = each layer's clip time scale with blend times in real seconds; interaction states blend with the pose weights during a fade (r6's fixed 12-frame ramp governs the states inside one clip)
options.change: global slow motion and/or the fixed 12-frame state ramp at transitions

decisions.recommended: cap the rest of P4 at about 4 h, then decide the combo clip (P3 remainder) and P5
decisions.facts: active time 39,560 s of 64,800 s at pause-24 (25,240 s left); P3 took about twice its estimate
